scheduled_change.what: Florida Building Code, 9th Edition (2026). Jacksonville's Building Inspection Division gives January 1, 2027 as the effective date (the Florida Building Commission's workplan gives December 31, 2026). No permits submitted under the 8th Edition are accepted after December 31, 2026; the division accepts permits submitted under the 9th Edition from December 1, 2026. Jacksonville's two local technical amendments were adopted for the 8th Edition; Ordinance 2023-780-E itself records that the earlier ones expired when the 8th Edition took effect, so they lapse with the 9th Edition unless the Council readopts them.
scheduled_change.quote: The Florida Building Code (FBC), 9th Edition (2026) takes effect on January 1, 2027. After December 31, 2026, no permits submitted under The Florida Building Code (FBC), 8th Edition (2023) will be accepted. The City of Jacksonville's Building Inspection Division will accept permits submitted under Florida Building Code, 9th Edition (2026) beginning December 1, 2026.

restrooms_city.rule: No city rule on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms was found. Jacksonville does add a rule on family rooms: Ordinance Code Section 321.111 (Ordinance 2023-780-E, a local technical amendment to Florida Building Code, Building, Section 1210.5) requires a family or assisted-use toilet room (a unisex accessible room with one water closet and one lavatory, a door securable from inside and an 'occupied' indicator) with an adult-changing table in a newly built or substantially renovated assembly or mercantile building with a restroom open to the public that is required to have an aggregate of six or more male or female water closets, unless the Building Codes Adjustment Board grants a variance. In a pre-existing structure the owner may instead fit an adult-changing table in an existing accessible stall in each room. Substantial renovation means work on more than 50 percent of the gross floor area that includes structural changes to an existing public toilet room. Section 321.103 separately requires baby-changing tables in listed buildings (not used on the page).
restrooms_city.quote: in any newly constructed Building, as defined in Section 321.111(a)(2), Ordinance Code, or any Building undergoing Substantial Renovation, as defined in Section 321.111(a)(5), Ordinance Code, which is required to have an aggregate of six or more male or female water closets, shall have available a Family or Assisted-Use Toilet Room, as defined in Section 321.111(a)(4), or when official codes require installation of bathing or showering facilities, a Family or Assisted-Use Bathing Room, as defined in Section 321.111(a)(3), with an Adult-Changing Table unless granted a variance by the Building Codes Adjustment Board, under Chapter 56, Ordinance Code. (i) As an alternative to the Family or Assisted-Use Toilet Room or Bathing Room, in a pre-existing structure the owner can adapt or retro-fit an existing accessible stall with an Adult-Changing Table in each room, allowing both men and women access to an Adult-Changing Table. (ii) Substitution of urinals for water closets does not relieve the obligation [...]
restrooms_city.definition_quote: (4) Family or Assisted-Use Toilet Room means a designated unisex accessible toilet facility with a minimum of one water closet and one lavatory. [...] The door to the Family or Assisted-Use Toilet Room shall be securable from within the room and be provided with an "occupied" indicator. (5) Substantial Renovation/Substantially Renovated means any reconstruction, rehabilitation, addition, or other improvement that involves more than 50 percent of the gross floor area occupied by the building, and that includes structural changes to any existing public toilet room.
restrooms_city.note: Read in the copy Jacksonville filed with the Florida Building Commission (ordinance text with certificate: enacted March 26, 2024, approved March 28, 2024) and in the Commission's report of local amendments to the 8th Edition. The section tells the Building Codes Adjustment Board to adopt the requirement by rule; the Board's rule itself was not found or read. One web search found no Jacksonville ordinance on single-user restroom signs or all-gender rooms; the Ordinance Code on Municode could not be opened, so that part is 'none found', not 'none exists'.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Jacksonville job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for coastal humidity and see the local rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Jacksonville offices, schools, hospitals and port warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Florida's plumbing rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and Jacksonville applies them unchanged. The table below shows what that means.
page.code_change_bullet: - **New rules on January 1, 2027:** Florida replaces its building rules with a new edition, and Jacksonville applies it from that day. The city takes permit applications under the current rules until December 31, 2026, and under the new edition from December 1, 2026.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Jacksonville's list of work that needs no permit covers patio slabs, replacing plumbing fixtures and small plumbing and equipment repairs, and doesn't name toilet partitions. The city says a permit is needed for construction that physically changes a property, alterations included. Ask the Jacksonville Building Inspection Division at 904-255-8500 whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** one-person and family restrooms must be marked as open to everyone. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and urinals are in stalls or screened from view. A 2023 Florida law sets separate rules for schools, colleges, jails and government buildings; private businesses aren't covered by it. Jacksonville adds a rule for theaters, restaurants, churches, arenas, stores and similar buildings with restrooms open to the public. If the building is new or substantially renovated and needs six or more toilets, it must have a family restroom with an adult changing table, and swapping toilets for urinals doesn't remove that duty. In an existing building the owner may fit an adult changing table in an accessible stall in each restroom instead. A renovation counts as substantial when it covers more than half the building's floor area and changes the structure of a public restroom.
page.stalls_after: In restaurants and other gathering places, Florida can require three women's toilets for every two men's toilets and urinals once the men's room has more than two. Licensed restaurants may be exempt, so confirm with the Jacksonville Building Inspection Division. Outdoor seating counts toward the number of people. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or the Jacksonville Building Inspection Division sets the final number.
page.install_rule: A contractor who pulls permits in Jacksonville registers with the Building Inspection Division first, with a Florida construction license and proof of workers' compensation cover or exemption. Contractors doing covered contracting work in Jacksonville need a valid contractor certificate from the city or the state. Florida has no state license category specifically for toilet partitions, and a contractor whose work falls in a licensed category needs that license, so confirm with the Building Inspection Division which one covers your job. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who pulls a permit in Jacksonville registers a Florida license with the city first.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Florida has no state wage law for public construction and doesn't let cities or school districts set one. On federally funded work the federal rate applies: $23.63 an hour plus $13.30 in benefits for a carpenter on building work in Duval County.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7.5% in Jacksonville: 6% state and 1.5% Duval County. The county's 1.5% applies only to the first $5,000 of each item.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals and medical offices:** phenolic or stainless steel that stands up to frequent cleaning, with privacy options for patient and staff restrooms.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023): Building, Plumbing and Accessibility volumes, in force since December 31, 2023; replaced by the 9th Edition (2026), which Jacksonville applies from January 1, 2027; Jacksonville Ordinance Code, Chapter 321 (Adoption of Building Code), Section 321.111, Family or Assisted-Use Toilet or Bathing Rooms (Ordinance 2023-780-E), a local technical amendment to Section 1210.5 of the Building volume; NFPA 286 for HDPE under the International Building Code, the model for Florida's code.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like replacement of anchored toilet partitions needs a Jacksonville permit (Building Inspection Division, 904-255-8500, BIDDocuments@coj.net).
The permit bullet rests on the division's FAQ lists, not the ordinance: read the exempt-work section of Ordinance Code Chapter 320 on Municode in a browser (automated access is blocked).
Update on January 1, 2027: the 9th Edition (2026) Florida Building Code applies in Jacksonville. Rewrite the 'New rules' bullet and recheck the stall table against the published 9th Edition.
Jacksonville's notice gives January 1, 2027 for the 9th Edition; the Florida Building Commission's workplan gives December 31, 2026. The page follows the city's notice.

Jacksonville's family-restroom rule (Section 321.111) is a local amendment to the 8th Edition. Ordinance 2023-780-E records that the earlier amendments expired when the 8th Edition took effect, so check before January 1, 2027 whether the Council has readopted it for the 9th Edition or the 9th Edition carries its own rule, and rewrite the restroom bullet.

Section 321.111 tells the Building Codes Adjustment Board to adopt the family-restroom requirement by rule; the Board's rule was not found. Ask the Building Inspection Division how it applies the section.
Jacksonville also requires baby-changing tables in listed new or substantially renovated buildings (Ordinance Code Section 321.103); it is left off the page because it doesn't affect stalls.

The Building Inspection Division covers the City of Jacksonville only: Jacksonville Beach, Atlantic Beach, Neptune Beach and Baldwin have their own building departments, and the division says it doesn't issue building permits for public school facilities.
No Jacksonville rule on single-user restroom signs or all-gender rooms was found, but the Ordinance Code could not be opened: check it once in a browser.
Sales tax: the Department of Revenue's 2026 publications announce no change for Duval County; read the 2027 Form DR-15DSS when the Department posts it.
The Department of Revenue doesn't say whether toilet partitions count as a building fixture or as goods, which decides how an installed job is taxed (same open question as Miami).
The Duval County carpenter rate in determination FL20260202 is a union rate dated August 1, 2020; recheck sam.gov for a newer modification before launch.
